findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Raw chicken was observed being stored over raw beef in the walk-in cooler in the kitchen. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) moved the chicken to be stored appropriately. Ensure that the proper storage order procedure is followed to avoid cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed three containers of tomato sauce with a label “Use First” without their production dates. The PIC was made aware. The PIC told inspector that the sauces were made a couple days before. Education was provided. The respective dates were added to teh containers immediately. Ensure that date marking guidelines are followed to the letter at all times.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Inspector observed jalapeños stored in an open can in the walk in cooler. The person in charge stated the can was opened yesterday. CORRECTED- education about storage of acidic foods in metal cans was conducted, and the jalapeños were transferred to a food safe container. Ensure acidic foods held past the day of opening are stored in a food safe container if held past one day, to ensure no metals leach into the food.
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.[P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed one container of cooked ground beef to bear the date 3/27, and another container to have no date in the walk in cooler. CORRECTED- the person in charge verified that the beef was cooked on Wednesday (4/1), and wrote the date to reflect. Ensure all temperature control for food safety items are marked with the day of preparation, to be used or discarded within seven days. The day of preparation/ thawing/ opening counts as day one.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed shrimp thawing in a metal container at room temperature. CORRECTED- the person in charge moved food under cold running water, which was later transferred to the prep table, to be cooked today. Ensure use of proper thawing methods, which includes placing the items under cold running water, moving to refrigeration, or cooking to the items to the minimum internal cooking temperature (145F for shrimp).
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F). [Pf]

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an unlabeled container of a white grainy substance. CORRECTED- staff confirmed the item as salt, and placed a label to reflect the containers contents. Ensure foods that may easily be mistaken for other foods and chemicals are labeled after removing from their original container to prevent contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed uncovered salsa verde and tomato sauces in the walk-in-cooler. Ensure ready-to-eat (RTE) foods are covered during storage to prevent contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings. [C]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed two bags of onions and tortillas in the rest room. CORRECTED- the PIC was informed and the onions and tortillas will be moved to a different location as soon as additional staff arrive. Ensure food is not stored in rest rooms to prevent contamination of foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.12(B) Food Storage, Prohibited Areas. Toilet Rooms. FOOD may not be stored: (B) In toilet rooms. [Pf]

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the triple sink faucet to be dripping water. Ensure leak is repaired by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair. (C)

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Fish was observed being stored over ready to eat (RTE) foods; hash browns, cheese, and washed vegetables in the prep cooler in the kitchen. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) moved the fish to be stored underneath RTE foods. Ensure RTE foods are always stored above meat. Inspector provided facility with a storage order graphic in Spanish.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: A wet sanitizer cloth was observed on the kitchen prep table. Education occurred regarding the storage of wet sanitizer cloths. Ensure sanitizer wiping cloths are stored in a sanitizer solution when not in use.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D). [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Employees were observed washing hands then using their newly-clean hands to turn the faucet off. CORRECTED- Inspector discussed proper handwashing with PIC, who will educate employees. Ensure a paper towel or other barrier is used to turn the faucet off to prevent recontaminating hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: 1st REPEAT: Raw chicken in a ziplock bag in a plastic tub was observed stored over raw beef in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- The raw chicken was sealed with no apparent leaks. PIC rearranged storage to keep chicken below other raw meats to prevent potential cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature.
findings.comment: A large pot of queso was observed in the walk-in cooler at 61F (probed). PIC indicated that the queso was cooked the previous night and had cooled briefly at room temperature before being moved to the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- PIC voluntarily discarded the queso. Ensure foods cool from 135F to 70F within 2 hours, and reach 41F in no more than 6 hours total.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.14(A) Cooling. (A) Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled: (1) Within 2 hours from 57C (135F) to 21C (70°F); and (2) Within a total of 6 hours from 57C (135F) to 5C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Queso, cooked last night, was observed in a large pot in the walk-in cooler. Queso did not meet the necessary cooling benchmarks. Cooling methods are inadequate. Inspector discussed dividing queso into smaller portions and using ice wands to speed up the cooling process. Cooling foods need to be monitored to ensure they cool quickly. Review cooling methods and procedures with staff. Inspector will provide additional education in Spanish.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.15(A) Cooling Methods. (A) Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of FOOD being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods. [Pf]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Daylight is visible along the floor/wall joint in both dry storage sheds. Seal both sheds along the floor/wall joints to prevent entry of pests.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
1) Wire shelving in the walk-in cooler has become rusted and soiled with debris. Clean shelving and resurface, seal, or replace as needed to eliminate the rust and ensure shelving is smooth and easily cleanable.
2) Plastic protective coating is present on the shelf above the steam table. Remove the plastic coating.
findings.citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. [C]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Facility is cooking in pots too large to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized in the facility’s 3 compartment sink. Pots need to be able to fit in the 3 compartment sinks to adequately be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. PIC will modify processes to use smaller pots that will fit in the sink basins.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.12(B) Manual Warewashing, Sink Compartment Requirements. (B) Sink compartments shall be large enough to accommodate immersion of the largest EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS. If EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS are too large for the WAREWASHING sink, a WAREWASHING machine or alternative EQUIPMENT as specified in (C) of this section shall be used. [Pf]

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Owner’s allergen awareness training certificate expired in October 2024. Two other CFMs have not completed allergen awareness training. Ensure all CFMs complete allergen awareness training.
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
No CFM was present at the beginning of this inspection. CORRECTED- PIC (a CFM) arrived shortly after the inspection began, after an employee called him. Ensure there is a CFM present any time food is being prepared or served.
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Employees observed donning gloves without washing hands first. Wash hands before donning gloves. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC and employees. Provided education.
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands. [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Thawing raw chicken was observed stored above raw beef in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- PIC rearranged storage so chicken is stored below or away from other raw meats to prevent potential cross contamination.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Foods in the prep cooler and walk-in cooler were observed without date-markings. Foods included portions of queso in the prep cooler, and black beans and tacos in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- Black beans were voluntarily discarded. PIC knew the tacos were prepared on Saturday and was confident they would all be sold today. The container was labeled to indicate prep on Saturday. The queso portion cups were from a bulk container in the walk-in cooler that was labeled. Date-labels need to follow the product as it moves through the facility. Ensure foods that will be held in the facility for more than 24 hours are labeled with the date they were prepared or opened.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1. (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date. (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food. (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container. (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma). [Pf]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Frozen churros were spilled in the small chest freezer, in contact with packages and the interior of the freezer itself. CORRECTED- PIC discarded the spilled churros. 
3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
The lid of the longer chest cooler is damaged and split along the front edge on the interior, exposing the insulation inside of the lid. Repair or replace the lid/cooler so that the lid is smooth and easily cleanable, and so that the gaps are eliminated.
4-101.11: Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Several bare wood shelves have been installed in the kitchen. Paint or otherwise seal the wood shelves so they are smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable.
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. [C]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Thawing raw chicken was observed stored above cilantro and other ready-to-eat foods in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- PIC rearranged storage so chicken is stored below or away from ready-to-eat foods.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment:
A 4-inch deep pan of white rice was observed at 67F (probed) in the bottom of the prep cooler. PIC stated that it was prepared yesterday. All other foods in the prep cooler were observed at or below 41F, therefore it was determined that the rice had not properly cooled after being prepared yesterday. CORRECTED- Improperly cooled rice was voluntarily discarded. Discussed cooling methods for rice (such as smaller portions and shallow pans). Use cooling methods and monitor cooling foods to ensure they move from 135F to 70F in 2 hours or less, and reach 41F within no more than 6 hours total.
3-501.14: (A) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within in 2 hours from 135F to 70F. Within 6 hours, FOOD shall cool from 135F to 41F or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Foods in the prep cooler and walk-in cooler were observed without date-markings. Foods included white rice in the prep cooler, and refried beans and two containers of birria in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- White rice and refried beans were voluntarily discarded (rice was improperly cooled; refried beans are typically prepared daily). Birria was prepared yesterday and was labeled accordingly. Ensure foods that will be held in the facility for more than 24 hours are labeled with the date they were prepared or opened.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1. (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date. (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food. (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container. (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma). [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
No ambient thermometer was present in the prep cooler. Ensure all cold holding units have ambient thermometers placed inside to monitor air temperature.
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. [C]

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.comment:
A container of white powder was observed unlabeled on the shelf below the drink dispenser. CORRECTED- PIC stated that the powder is flour and labeled it accordingly. Ensure foods that may be easily mistaken are labeled to avoid confusion or misuse.
3-302.12: If in working container, FOOD not readily recognized or easily mistakable shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Tortilla chips were observed store uncovered directly next to the handwashing sink. Discussed protecting the chips from potential splash from the handwashing sink. CORRECTED- PIC added a lid to the container to protect the chips.
3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306. [C]

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Single service forks near the cash register are stored mixed directions (fork ends and handles are intermixed). Store single service utensils so that only the handles are touched by employees.
4-904.11: (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. [C]

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
There are multiple small holes in the walls behind the 3 compartment sink and behind the freezers. Seal the holes in the walls.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
No CFM was present at the beginning of this inspection. CORRECTED- PIC (a CFM) arrived shortly after the inspection began, after an employee called him. Ensure there is a CFM present any time food is being prepared or served.
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
1) 1st REPEAT: A tub of cooked pork was observed at 66F (probed) on the kitchen counter. Employees stated that the pork was removed from the walk-in cooler at 7am (about 1.5 hours prior to the temperature observations) with the intention of portioning it into bags and freezing it. The facility was out of bags so the pork was returned to the walk-in cooler. When the temperature was checked again at 10:30am, the pork was 65F (probed) and was voluntarily discarded. Only remove foods from cold-holding when ready to work with them. Do not store foods on the countertops (out of refrigeration) for extended periods of time. (Previously observed 9/22/23).
2) Shell eggs in the top of the prep cooler were observed with an ambient temperature of 51F, and an internal temperature of 54F (probed) when an egg was cracked. CORRECTED- About 1.5 dozen eggs were voluntarily discarded. All other foods in the prep cooler were 41F or below.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
1) A container of salsa going into the prep cooler was observed with a date marking of 5/3, making 5/9 the last day the salsa could be served. CORRECTED- PIC voluntarily discarded the salsa. Foods must be used or discarded within 7 days of prep, with the day prepared counting as Day 1 (the day prepared +6 days).
2) A container of pork was observed with its date label reading “pollo rojo.” Several other containers in the walk-in cooler were similarly mislabeled, causing confusion regarding the accuracy of the date labels (though all dates were in the appropriate time frame, the foods did not correspond with the contents of the container). Ensure labels are removed from containers in the warewashing process, and that foods are labeled with the date they were opened or prepared. CORRECTED- Containers were relabeled to reflect their contents and prep dates.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1. [Pf]

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
Frozen shrimp was observed in a pan of water on the counter. The shrimp was still about 41F on the surface, and frozen in parts. After reviewing thawing methods, PIC moved the shrimp to the walk-in cooler to continue thawing. Thaw foods under cool running water or in the refrigerator.
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service. [C]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Tortilla chips were observed store uncovered directly next to the handwashing sink. Discussed protecting the chips from potential splash from the handwashing sink. CORRECTED- PIC added a lid to the container to protect the chips.
3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306. [C]

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Boxes of single service napkins and to-go containers were observed stored directly on the floor in the small storage shed. Store single-service items at least 6 inches above the floor to facilitate cleaning and prevent pest harborage.
4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
The lid of the longer chest cooler is damaged and split along the front edge on the interior, exposing the insulation inside of the lid. Repair or replace the lid/cooler so that the lid is smooth and easily cleanable, and so that the gaps are eliminated.
4-101.11: Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. [C]

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
One employee’s food handler certificate expired in April 2024. Ensure employees renew food handler certificates as they expire. Keep current food handler certificates on file for all employees.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement. [C]
